correctness.rationale: The normalized midpoint matrix is an exactly orthogonal Cayley rotation with angle 2 arctan t. Its second complex harmonic Z(t)=((1+it)/(1-it))^2 exactly multiplies the traceless second moment, so E Z=0 iff universal one-step isotropy; the trace is fixed by energy conservation. The exact identity t-(1-Re Z-Im Z)/2=t(t-1)^2(t^2+2t+3)/(1+t^2)^2 >= 0 proves E t >= 1/2 over all nonnegative integrable laws. Equality forces t in {0,1}, and E Z=0 fixes weights 1/2 each. The constructed quarter-turn pair solves every strictly supercritical prescribed mean. Semicircle separation proves both support caps. Actual packaged verify.py was executed successfully with SymPy, checking the rational identities, the update orthogonality, the two-point law and second-moment formulas. Finite checks do not substitute for the analytic universal inequality. Limits: fixed-frequency planar oscillator, exact arithmetic and uncentered second moments (centered covariance only for initially zero-mean ensembles).

originality.rationale: The exact jointly sharp mean-duration, equality-law and hard-cap frontier for universal one-step harmonic second-moment isotropization was not implied by the full-text passages inspected in the motivating random-step ODE paper or related HMC jittering paper. The strongest directly indexed harmonic second-moment source studies stochastic-forcing stationary bias, not the phase-cancellation criterion. Established midpoint energy preservation and elementary Fourier/rotation relations are not new; the contribution is the global moment-law extremal characterization. Equivalence with unindexed optimal phase-randomization remains a genuine priority risk.
residual_risks: Potential equivalent optimal quadrupole/second-harmonic cancellation inequality in unpublished or unindexed literature was not ruled out; originality is a bounded self-review, not certification.
The method is a coarse random-time benchmark. Canceling second moments is not full phase uniformity or control of numerical trajectory accuracy.

value.rationale: An isotropic second-moment benchmark measures elimination of orientation bias in ensemble harmonic dynamics while exactly preserving energy; unlike arbitrary finite tabulations, it is a natural invariant-based distributional design objective. The theorem proves the sharp minimum mean physical timestep, uniqueness of the optimizer, attainment for all larger strictly positive mean durations and a distinct sharp maximum-permitted-duration feasibility frontier. These give exact limitations on random-time geometric integration and phase mixing despite the source method permitting arbitrary distributions. Scope is explicitly not optimization of trajectory error or numerical work.
